description: geoclaw-landspill is an open-source package for simulating the overland flow of oil released by pipeline ruptures, for use in pipeline risk management. It was written by Pi-Yueh Chuang, Tracy Thorleifson and Lorena A. Barba, and its numerical solver is a modified version of GeoClaw, which solves the full shallow-water equations. Additions include point sources for rupture points, evaporation models, Darcy-Weisbach bottom friction with land roughness, temperature-dependent viscosity, and records of where and when oil flows into inland waterbodies, with pre- and post-processing utilities. The method is location-independent, but automatic download of topography and hydrology data works only for the United States. It is a Python package with a Fortran solver, installed through conda from the barbagroup channel or through pip with gfortran, and Docker and Singularity containers are provided; results are CF-1.7 NetCDF files. It is licensed under BSD-3-Clause at no cost, reviewed in the Journal of Open Source Software, and version 1.0 is archived on Zenodo (June 2021). Caveats: only Linux is supported, and the last commit dates from June 2021. Simulation uses are spill hazard exposure mapping along pipeline routes and emergency response planning.
